title: Opal Summit — Enterprise Outreach Cribsheet
content:
Notes to self — quick reference for Opal Summit outreach (rough).

Account snapshot:
- Company: Opal Summit (mid-market retail analytics + CRM)
- HQ: Chicago, US; 500–800 employees; growing ML team (2 ICs + 1 manager listed on LinkedIn)
- Likely infra constraints: tight data compliance for customer PII, on-prem analytics pipelines, preference for private VPC options
- Current stack hints: Postgres + Snowflake, internal microservices on GKE, experimental with vector DBs (Pinecone mention in job posts)

Primary hypothesis / pain to test:
- They are building in-product insights and agent workflows that require predictable token cost and low tail latency.
- Need better inference economics than naive cloud-hosted endpoints (batching/kv cache would help).
- Security/regulatory: likely want VPC or Private option for PII-sensitive prompts.

Potential use cases (quick shortlist):
1) Real-time chat assistant for merchant support (low-latency, high availability)
2) SKU recommendation + reranking (embedding + rerank; cost sensitive)
3) Summarization of call transcripts (bursty, long-context)

Key contacts to find / verify:
- ML Platform / Head of Data Science (target) — likely champion for infra control
- Head of Product (target for use-case buy-in)
- Security/Compliance lead (necessary for Private/VPC convo)
- Eng manager for customer-facing services (practical constraints)

Quick discovery script (for first intro call / intro email):
- 30s opener: "We help product teams run LLM features in production with predictable latency and unit economics — without building the whole inference stack. Would love to share a couple ideas after a short discovery.
- Questions to surface:
  * Which LLM workloads are highest priority for next 6 months? realtime chat, summarization, embeddings?
  * Rough QPS/peak concurrency and SLOs (p50/p95 latency targets)?
  * Any blockers: security, cost, latency spikes, poor model reliability?
  * Are you open to a pilot with dedicated capacity or do you need a private VPC/on-prem setup?

Outreach sequence (multichannel, 3-week window):
- Day 0: Short intro email (see templates below) + LinkedIn connection message.
- Day 3: Follow-up email (value add: a one-pager on cost model + Redwood Optimize tip).
- Day 8: Voice mail + succinct voice message if reachability.
- Day 12: Second follow-up with suggested times and 15-20 min discovery.
- Day 20: Last check with short product demo invite (recorded 6-min demo link).

A/B subject line experiments (test concurrently):
A. "Reduce LLM latency & token cost for Opal Summit’s support AI"
B. "15-minute plan to make your chat assistant <50ms p95"

Draft cold email (concise — version A):
Hi {{first_name}},

I work with product teams building chat and recommendation features. We help them get predictable p95 latency and ~2–5x lower token spend per session (prefix caching + batching) without a big ops lift.

If you’re exploring cost/latency fixes for any in-product assistants or rerank pipelines, could we schedule a 15-min discovery next week? I can share a short pilot plan that respects PII and VPC requirements.

— Avery

Follow-up email (value add):
- Include quick bullet: "How we cut median token cost by 40% for a commerce customer (dedicated caching + model routing)."
- Attach one-pager or link to demo (internal: INF-3421 deck).

Objection handling (cheat sheet):
- "We own our data / cannot send PII to hosted API": Redwood Private + VPC solution + KMS support, offer audit log sample and compliance checklist. Ask what data classification looks like and propose a small scope pilot with masked PII.
- "We already host models ourselves": acknowledge, probe pain: maintenance, long tail latency, cost. Pitch Redwood as a runtime that can sit on-prem / in customer VPC and replace home-grown serving with better KV caching and rollout controls.
- "Cost too high / no budget": propose time-boxed pilot with measurable success metric (e.g., 30% token cost reduction or meeting p95 latency SLO). Offer a short term credit or trial capacity (sales play).
- "Latency spikes when load increases": explain smart routing + autoscale policies + dedicated pools to stabilize p95; offer metrics from similar deployments.

Technical fit checklist (for discovery call) — quick YES/NO items to capture:
- Expected max concurrency / QPS?
- Current model sizes / architectures in use (e.g., Llama2, Mistral, custom)?
- Do you need on-prem or is VPC acceptable?
- Data residency/regulatory constraints?
- Do you have an existing embedding index (vector DB)? Which one?
- Any SLA/uptime requirements we should know (SRE involvement)?

Pilot plan (starter, 6 weeks):
- Week 0: kickoff, scope one vertical (support-chat or rerank) — define success metric (p95 latency < X ms, cost per session -30%).
- Week 1–2: infra setup — choose Hosted/Dedicated/Private; connect minimal dataset (masked), run smoke tests.
- Week 3–4: optimize runtime (batching, KV cache configuration), telemetry + evals.
- Week 5: A/B quality check vs baseline + cost analysis.
- Week 6: wrap + rollout proposal or handoff to eng team.

Success metrics we should propose upfront (pick 1–2):
- p95 latency target for chat (ms)
- % reduction in token spend for a common session
- Throughput improvement (requests/sec) for peak windows

Attachments to prepare before outreach:
- 1-pager: "Redwood pilot for Opal Summit" (high-level scope + SSO/VPC notes) — link to draft in GH PR 42
- 6-min recorded demo (hosted link)
- Compliance checklist + example audit log (trimmed)

Open questions / follow-ups (notes to self):
- Confirm whether Opal Summit has any active contracts with vector DB vendors (Pinecone / Weaviate?) — job posts hinted at Pinecone.
- Find exact names for security lead (LinkedIn) and tag them in Confluence note.
- Get a recent case study to cite for retail customer (token cost reduction example).

Quick call script (2–3 minute opening for intro call):
- Intro (20s): "Avery from Redwood — we help teams run LLM features at predictable latency/cost. I saw you’re building X — curious about your current plan for serving inference in prod."
- Discovery (60s): 2–3 quick questions: workload types, p95 target, blockers.
- Close (20s): propose pilot or quick follow-up: "If there’s alignment, I’ll share a 6-week pilot we run with other retail teams — low-effort and measurable."

Immediate next tasks (TODOS):
- Draft 1-pager and link into this doc (owner: Avery) — due 2025-09-18.
- Get compliance checklist from Security (tag Jordan).
- Run A/B email subject test: send 50 sample emails between 9/15–9/19, track open/click.

Rough pm notes / mental model: keep outreach lightweight and test two value props: cost reduction vs latency/SLO reliability. Different personas care differently — product/ML = cost/quality, security = VPC/compliance, eng = ops/observability.

End of cribsheet. Keep lean; reuse in other mid-market retail accounts but swap specifics.
